## 1 · Count or rate?

| | Meaning | Use |
|---|---|---|
| **Count** | events (cases) | workload |
| **Rate** | events / **person-time** | risk, comparisons |
| **Rate ratio** | rate in group A / rate in group B | effect measure |

City rate: **34.3 per 100,000 person-months**. Always name the **denominator** (person-months, person-years).

## 2 · Which model?

| Situation | Model | R |
|---|---|---|
| Counts, variance about = mean | **Poisson** | `glm(y ~ x + offset(log(pt)), family = poisson)` |
| Overdispersed, SEs only | **Quasi-Poisson** | `family = quasipoisson` |
| Overdispersed (usual) | **Negative binomial** | `MASS::glm.nb(y ~ x + offset(log(pt)))` |
| Structural zeros | **Zero-inflated / hurdle** | `pscl::zeroinfl(y ~ x | z, dist = "negbin")` |
| Repeated units | **Robust SE** | `lmtest::coeftest(m, vcov = sandwich::vcovCL(m, cluster = id))` |
| Common yes/no outcome, want PR | **Poisson + robust SE** | `glm(y01 ~ x, family = poisson)` + `vcovCL` |

## 3 · The offset

`offset(log(person-time))` makes exp(b) a **rate ratio**. Forget it and you compare **counts**, mixing risk with population size.

## 4 · Reading the output

| Result | How to say it |
|---|---|
| exp(b) = **0.66** (0.54-0.80) for fogging | "the **rate** was about 34% lower (adjusted)" |
| exp(100 b) = **1.41** per 100 mm of rain | "41% higher rate per extra 100 mm" |
| CI includes 1 | no clear association |
| `predict(type = "response")` | **expected counts** (log scale by default) |

## 5 · Checking

| Check | Poisson here | Good if |
|---|---|---|
| **Dispersion** (Pearson chi-square / df) | **7.9** | about 1 |
| **AIC**: Poisson vs NB | 10745 vs 5898 | lower is better |
| **Zeros**: observed vs expected | 20% vs 19% (NB) | close |
| **Fit over time**, **autocorrelation** | `acf(residuals(m, "pearson"))` | no pattern |

## 6 · Pitfalls

::: {.bad}
- **No offset** when populations or follow-up differ; a rate ratio read as a **risk or odds ratio**
- **Poisson CIs** reported for **overdispersed** data
- **Ignoring season and trend**, **clustering** or **autocorrelation**
- Zero-inflation added **without asking why**; **zero-truncated** data analysed as ordinary counts
- **Ecological** results read as individual effects; **association read as cause**
:::

## 7 · One-paragraph report

*Across 30 wards and 36 months (1,080 ward-months; 10,411 dengue cases) the data were overdispersed (Poisson dispersion 7.9), so negative binomial regression with a ward-population offset was used, with clustered robust standard errors. After adjustment for ward type, previous-month rainfall, time trend and seasonality, the dengue rate in fogged ward-months was 0.66 times that in unfogged ward-months (95% CI 0.54-0.80).*

:::
